content.text:
The scrollbar thumb is now filled only slightly lighter than its track, with a 1px border that stands out more. All tests pass (174, 1 ignored), but I haven't seen it on screen: my screenshot caught your browser instead of the app.

- **Fill:** the track colour nudged a little towards the theme's text colour, 8% in dark mode and 6% in light mode. So it's slightly lighter than the track in dark mode and slightly darker in light mode. Before, it was a half-transparent grey.
- **Border:** the same nudge but stronger, 28% in dark mode and 22% in light mode, so in dark mode it's brighter than the fill. The thumb is still a square-cornered rectangle filling the track's width.

Since this is shared code, every scrollbar in the app changes. If it's too subtle or too strong once you see it, those four percentages in `thumb_colors` in `src/scrollbar.rs` are the only values to tweak.

A new unit test checks that on a dark track the fill is only a little lighter and the border clearly brighter, and that on a light track both go darker. Scrollbar behaviour is unchanged, and its tests still pass.

The spec's `track` section in `spec/ui/components/scrollbar/index.pi` now describes the fill and border. `piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` ran cleanly, and the app builds with no warnings.
